# Runner's alacritty snapshot accessors

Upstream: published `alacritty_terminal` 0.26.0, copied from Cargo's registry source, with its license and packaged files unchanged. The generated registry cache marker `.cargo-ok` is omitted. Jason authorized this accessor-only exception on 2026-10-05 for #645 mission 1b.

Only `src/term/mod.rs` differs from the published source. It adds public `SnapshotState<'a>` and `Term::snapshot_state(&self) -> SnapshotState<'_>`. Every field is borrowed and read-only: `inactive_grid`, `scroll_region`, `title`, `title_stack`, `tabs`, `keyboard_mode_stack`, `inactive_keyboard_mode_stack`, `active_charset`, and `cursor_style`. The optional cursor style preserves whether Runner settings still control the default; serializing the resolved style freezes it and breaks the existing configure test. The selected charset is required to continue DEC line drawing after attach, even when the G0–G3 definitions are identical. Jason confirmed that additional read-only state needed by the split-point gate is authorized. Runner's VT snapshot must preserve these fields on attach; upstream's rendering API exposes only the active grid and current modes. No existing logic, mutable API, parsing or terminal behavior changes.

On upgrade, replace this tree with the new published crate and its license files, excluding `.cargo-ok`, then re-apply this one struct and getter beside `Term`. Check upstream field names and types, compare every other packaged file byte for byte, and run Runner's snapshot round-trip and split-point corpus tests. Record `diff -ru` against the installed registry source; the only differences must be the additions listed here and this document.
